lines.japanese: 学校──視野を広げるに当たり、これほど相応しい場所はないだろう。
lines.english: School—what place could be more appropriate for broadening one's perspective?

lines.japanese: 「さあいくぞ、薔薇色の学び舎へ！」
lines.english: “Onward, to the rose-colored halls of learning!”

lines.japanese: 三学期初日。きっと今日からまた、素晴らしい学園生活が待っているに違いない。
lines.english: It was the first day of the third term. Another magnificent chapter of school life surely awaited me.

lines.japanese: 「おはようみんな！」
lines.english: “Good morning, everyone!”

lines.japanese: 跳ねたくなるような気持ちを声に乗せ、俺は教室へ飛びこんだ。
lines.english: Putting enough cheer in my voice to skip down the halls, I burst into the classroom.

lines.japanese: しかし同級生たちの反応は淡泊だった。
lines.english: My classmates' response, however, was lukewarm.

lines.japanese: ああそうか、俺たち受験生だもんな。いまの時期は多少ピリピリした空気にもなるよな。
lines.english: Oh, of course. We were college applicants. The atmosphere was bound to be a little tense at this time of year.

lines.japanese: 呑気な顔でいられるのは、よっぽど余裕があるか、すでに進路が決まってる生徒ぐらいか。
lines.english: Only the supremely confident or those who had already settled their plans for next year could afford to look carefree.

lines.japanese: たとえばそう、秋も終わらぬうちからさっさと校内推薦枠を勝ちとっていた、あの女のような。
lines.english: Someone, for instance, like that woman who had snapped up an internal recommendation before autumn was even over.

lines.japanese: やつの名は渡来明日香。普段は賑やかな彼女の机だが、今朝は誰も集まってないみたいだ。
lines.english: Her name was Asuka Watarai. Her desk was usually bustling, but no one seemed to have gathered around it this morning.

lines.japanese: 渡来明日香、か……ふーむ、出掛けに女子とのレンアイなんてことを考えた矢先に遭遇したのがこの女とは、なんたる奇縁。
lines.english: Asuka Watarai... Hmm. What strange fate that I should encounter her just after contemplating romance with a woman on my way out.

lines.japanese: そういやタカシだった俺は、このお姫さまに対してレンアイに近い憧れを寄せていたんだよな。
lines.english: When I was Takashi, I had admired this princess with something approaching romantic feeling.

lines.japanese: だったら、いまの俺にも、素養は残ってるかもしれない。ちょっと意識を変えれば、彼女と青春くさい関係を育めるのではないだろうか。
lines.english: Perhaps I still had it in me. With a slight change in perspective, couldn’t I strike up some cheesy young romance with her?

lines.japanese: よし、では行ってみよう。
lines.english: All right. Let's give it a try.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう、渡来さん！」
lines.english: “Good morning, Watarai!”

lines.japanese: びっくりするほど無視された。
lines.english: She ignored me with almost impressive thoroughness.

lines.japanese: 「あれれ？　返事がないぞ？　ああそうか、本に夢中で聞こえなかったのかな」
lines.english: “Hmm? No answer? Oh, I see. You were so absorbed in your book that you didn't hear me.”

lines.japanese: 「よし、それじゃもう一度行くぞ。いいか？　これ冬休み明け一発目の大切な挨拶だからな。これで三学期の俺たちの関係が決まると言っても、過言じゃないぞ」
lines.english: “All right, let's try that again. Ready? This is our first important greeting after winter break. It is no exaggeration to say this moment will define our relationship for the entire third term.”

lines.japanese: 俺はボケッと呆けていた渡来明日香に、人付き合いのなんたるかを優しく説いた。
lines.english: I gently explained the fundamentals of human interaction to the vacant Asuka Watarai.

lines.japanese: 「はい、それじゃもう分かっただろ？　二週間ぶりなんだから、元気よくいこうね、さん、はいっ！」
lines.english: “Okay, you understand now, right? It's been two whole weeks, so let's put some spirit into it. And a-one, and a-two!”

lines.japanese: 「おはよう渡来さん！」
lines.english: “Good morning, Watarai!”

lines.japanese: またしても返事はなかった。
lines.english: Once again, no reply.

lines.japanese: 「な、なにこれ？　なんだ、もしかして俺はスルーされてるのか？　おうい、どうしたんだ渡来明日香。君の大好きなぱね田ぱね夫くんが朝の挨拶してるんだよ？」
lines.english: “Wh-what's going on? Are you ignoring me? Hellooo, Asuka Watarai. Paneda Paneo, the boy you adore, is saying good morning.”

lines.japanese: 「渡来さん。君は俺が大好きなはずだから、三学期初日、久しぶりに会った俺に泣きながら抱きついてくるはずなんだ」
lines.english: “Watarai. Since you love me, you should greet me on the first day of term by throwing your arms around me in tears after our long separation.”

lines.japanese: 「分かったね？　じゃあ今度こそきちんといくよ？　せーのっ、はい！」
lines.english: “Got it? Let's do it properly this time. Ready, set, go!”

lines.japanese: 「おはよう、渡来さん！」
lines.english: “Good morning, Watarai!”

lines.japanese: とことんプリンセスからの返事はなかった。
lines.english: Still the princess gave me no answer.

lines.japanese: 「終わった」
lines.english: “It's over.”

lines.japanese: そして勝手に語りはじめた。
lines.english: Then she began talking entirely on her own terms.

lines.japanese: 「冬休みが終わってしまった」
lines.english: “Winter break is over.”

lines.japanese: ああ、今日から三学期だからな。
lines.english: Yes. The third term began today.

lines.japanese: 「当初の予定だと、私は冬休み最後の日にちょっと遠出して、近代美術館の彫刻展を見るはずだった」
lines.english: “According to the original plan, I was going to venture a little farther afield on my last day of winter break and see the sculpture exhibition at the Museum of Modern Art.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、彫刻展！　そりゃまた高尚な休日を……ってあれ？　いま近代美術館でそんなのやってたか？」
lines.english: “A sculpture exhibition? What a cultured way to spend the day... Wait, is the museum even holding one right now?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ思いだした。彫刻展とか言うから知的に感じたけど、今やってるのアレだろ。『世界の珍獣大集合！　おもしろ動物の剥製展』」
lines.english: “Oh, I remember. Calling it sculpture made it sound intellectual, but you mean that exhibit they're running now: ‘Weird Beasts of the World! A Hilarious Taxidermy Menagerie.’”

lines.japanese: 「美術館の帰り道。アンビエントのＣＤなどを買いつつ、喫茶店で優雅に紅茶を嗜む予定だった」
lines.english: “On my way home from the museum, I planned to buy an ambient CD or two, then savor tea elegantly at a café.”

lines.japanese: 「なのに起きたら流れていた曲は、豆腐屋さんのラッパの音だった」
lines.english: “Yet when I awoke, the music drifting through the air was the tofu seller's horn.”

lines.japanese: 「それってバリバリ夕方だろ。ああ、寝てたのか」
lines.english: “That's late afternoon. Oh, you slept through the day.”

lines.japanese: 「優雅に紅茶を飲むはずが、テーブルの上に乗っていたのは、お湯と分離してもはや飲み物とは呼べないココアだった」
lines.english: “In place of the elegant tea I was to drink, the table held cocoa that had separated from the hot water so completely it could no longer be called a beverage.”

lines.japanese: 「ははあ、つまり周りのみんなが冬休み最後の日を有意義に過ごしている間、おまえは太陽が沈むころまで爆睡して、一日を無駄に過ごしたと」
lines.english: “Ah, I see. While everyone else made good use of the final day of winter break, you slept until sunset and wasted the whole thing.”

lines.japanese: 「返せよ」
lines.english: “Give it back.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「返せよ時間泥棒。私のスローライフを返せよう」
lines.english: “Give it back, you thief of time. Give me back my life of leisure.”

lines.japanese: 「し、知るか馬鹿。俺の体を揺するな、一日くらい休養したと思って諦めろ」
lines.english: “Like hell! Quit shaking me, idiot. Tell yourself you got a day of rest and let it go.”

lines.japanese: 「私の一週間返せよう！」
lines.english: “Give me back my whole week!”

lines.japanese: 「一週間かよ！」
lines.english: “It was a week?!”

lines.japanese: どんだけぐうたら宮廷ライフを送ったんだ、このプリンセスは。
lines.english: Just how indolent a life at court had this princess been living?

lines.japanese: 「ていうか、毎日夕方に起きてたのか」
lines.english: “Wait, you woke up in the evening every day?”

lines.japanese: 「ま、毎日じゃないよ。ちょっと大げさに言ってみただけだよね」
lines.english: “N-not every day. I exaggerated a little for effect.”

lines.japanese: この期に及んでしょーもない見栄を……。
lines.english: Petty vanity, even at this stage...

lines.japanese: 「そんなことよりどうしてくれるの私の冬休み」
lines.english: “Never mind that. What are you going to do about my winter break?”

lines.japanese: もはや言いがかりとさえ呼べない、単なる八つ当たりだった。
lines.english: This could no longer even be called a false accusation. She was simply taking her anger out on me.

lines.japanese: まったく冗談じゃない。冬休み中ゴロ寝するわ、不条理なイチャモンは付けるわ、おまけに暴力まで振るいやがる……とんでもない不良物件じゃないか、この女。
lines.english: What a terrible joke. She spent winter break lazing around, picked irrational fights, and even resorted to violence. This woman was a catastrophically bad prospect.

lines.japanese: こんなのと一緒にいたら、愛が芽生える前にまず命を落としかねん。俺の恋愛候補リストから、即刻その名をデリートしておこう。
lines.english: If I stayed with her, I was liable to lose my life before love had time to bloom. I would delete her name from my list of romantic prospects immediately.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう二人とも。ふふ、今日も元気そうで羨ましいな」
lines.english: “Good morning, you two. Heehee. I envy how energetic you are today.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、おはよう山科。どしたの、そっちは元気なさそうだね」
lines.english: “Oh, morning, Yamashina. What's wrong? You look kind of listless.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、せっかく冬休み最後の日は外人墓地で過ごそうと思ってたのに、一日布団の中で過ごしちゃったんだ。はあ……それだけの時間を無駄にすると、体中から気力みたいなものが抜けおちていくよね」
lines.english: “Yes. I meant to spend the final day of winter break at the foreign cemetery, but instead I spent the whole day in bed. Sigh... When you waste that much time, it feels as if all the energy drains out of you.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あんたもかいボーダーガール。俺も昨日は幽体離脱にハマっててなァ。一日をベッドの上で無駄にしてイラついてんだ。どっかに八つ当たりできる相手いねえかなァ」
lines.english: “Oh, you too, Borderline Girl? I got hooked on astral projection yesterday. Wasted the whole day in bed and now I'm pissed off. Wonder if there's somebody around I can take it out on.”

lines.japanese: いねえよ。
lines.english: There isn't.

lines.japanese: ていうか……みんな、時間は有効に使おうよ……。
lines.english: Seriously... Everybody, please make better use of your time...

lines.japanese: 昼休み。俺たち羽田班は、四人で共に昼食を取っていた。
lines.english: At lunch, the four members of Team Haneda ate together.

lines.japanese: 「ねえ、渡らないさん」
lines.english: “Say, Miss Wata-don't.”

lines.japanese: 「なに、ぱね田くん」
lines.english: “What is it, Paneda?”

lines.japanese: 「時にチミは、恋などしたことはあるかね？」
lines.english: “Tell me, my good lady: have you ever been in love?”

lines.japanese: 渡来明日香は一瞬硬直した。
lines.english: Asuka Watarai froze for an instant.

lines.japanese: 「……え、なに、恋？　コレ、何のネタ振り？」
lines.english: “...What? Love? What kind of setup is this?”

lines.japanese: 「はっ！　もしかしてぱね田くん、私のこと……」
lines.english: “Wait! Paneda, do you mean... you have feelings for me?”

lines.japanese: 「口から玉子焼きはみ出てるよ」
lines.english: “You've got omelet sticking out of your mouth.”

lines.japanese: 「や、やだな、ぱじゅかしい。てへっ☆」
lines.english: “Oh, no. How embawassing. Teehee☆”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、無理するんじゃない。地がはみ出てるぞ」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha. Don't force it. Your real self is showing.”

lines.japanese: 「で、どうしてそんな質問？」
lines.english: “So why the question?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん……」
真顔で聞きかえされても困るな……どうしてってこともなく、とりあえず意識改革として、なんとなくコイバナっぽい空気に触れてみたかっただけなんだけど。
lines.english: A straight-faced question was hard to answer. There was no particular reason. As part of changing my outlook, I had simply wanted to dip a toe into the atmosphere of romantic gossip.

lines.japanese: 「ああ……みんなは、どんな恋愛してるのかなーと思って」
lines.english: “I was just wondering... what kind of love lives everybody has.”

lines.japanese: とりあえず、俺が話の中心にされては困るので、一般論にしてみた。
lines.english: For the time being, I made it a general question so the conversation wouldn't center on me.

lines.japanese: 「へえ、なんでそんなこと……あ、もしかして“ぱね田くんが”恋愛のことで悩んでる？　それなら面白そうだから、話だけは聞いてあげるよ」
lines.english: “Huh. Why would you... Wait, is Paneda having romantic troubles? That sounds entertaining, so I'll at least hear you out.”

lines.japanese: く、くそっ、戻ってきた……。
lines.english: D-damn it. It came right back to me...

lines.japanese: ならばこの際だ、使いふるされた手を使ってさりげなく相談してみよう。
lines.english: Fine. Then I would try that timeworn trick and ask for advice indirectly.

lines.japanese: 「これは俺の話じゃないんだけど……たとえば自分も好きで、相手も好きだって言ってくれてるのに、事情があって付きあえない場合があるとするだろ」
lines.english: “This isn't about me, but... suppose two people like each other and have both said so, yet circumstances prevent them from being together.”

lines.japanese: 俺は自らの現状を、名もなき誰かのそれに置きかえて説明した。
lines.english: I recast my own situation as that of some nameless stranger.

lines.japanese: 「そういう位置に立たされたら、どう思うか聞いてみた──」
lines.english: “I wanted to know how somebody in that position might feel—”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ」
lines.english: “Hah.”

lines.japanese: 隣りで失笑が起こった。
lines.english: A derisive laugh came from beside me.
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 「純愛だねえ。いやいや、美しいなァと思っただけだ」
lines.english: “True love, huh? No, no. I was just thinking how beautiful it all sounds.”

lines.japanese: 針生蔵人は意味ありげに俺の目を見て笑う。
lines.english: Kuroudo Hariu looked meaningfully into my eyes and smiled.

lines.japanese: 「いや、俺の話じゃない。ていうかアレか？　あんたなら、さっさと他いくのか？」
lines.english: “This isn't about me. Anyway, what? You'd just move on to somebody else?”

lines.japanese: 好きあっているのに付きあえない男女。ひとつ所に留まらない主義の針生蔵人には、聞くまでもない愚問だったか。
lines.english: A man and woman who loved each other but couldn't be together. Perhaps asking a wanderer like Kuroudo was foolish from the start.

lines.japanese: しかし返答は、意外や柔軟なものだった。
lines.english: Yet his answer was surprisingly flexible.

lines.japanese: 「さあ、どうだろうなァ。相手にもよるんじゃないの。自分が一生かけられるような相手なら……ん、んンっ、待つのもひとつの手だろうし」
lines.english: “Who knows? Depends on the person, doesn't it? If they're somebody you'd give your whole life to... Ahem. Waiting might be one way to go.”

lines.japanese: 「待つのに疲れて一生を棒に振る可能性もあるけどね」
lines.english: “You could also grow tired of waiting and throw your whole life away.”

lines.japanese: ぬるりと割りこんできたのは、元来あまり他人に反論することなどない山科京だ。
lines.english: Miyako Yamashina—ordinarily one of the last people to contradict anyone—slid smoothly into the conversation.

lines.japanese: 俺と渡来明日香は、微妙な空気の揺らぎを感じて強張った。
lines.english: Asuka Watarai and I stiffened at the subtle shift in the air.

lines.japanese: 「『しばらく距離を置こう』なんて、呪いの言葉みたいなものだからね。相手の気持ちを繋ぎとめつつ、いつでも声かけられる位置へ置くには、便利な呪文だよ」
lines.english: “‘Let's spend some time apart’ is practically a curse. It's a convenient spell for keeping hold of somebody's feelings while leaving them close enough to call back whenever you want.”

lines.japanese: 「うわあ」
lines.english: “Whoa.”

lines.japanese: な、なんだろー、真に迫ってるなあ山科京。ま、まるで実体験みたいだぞー、はははー。
lines.english: W-wow, Yamashina sounded awfully convincing. A-almost as though she were speaking from experience. Ha ha ha...

lines.japanese: 「そうやって一本の糸へ縋りついてる相手のことなんて考えずに、自分はさっさと他の相手を見つけて、幸せになって……そんなの許せるわけないよ。だけど文句を言う権利なんて、どこにもないんだ」
lines.english: “You give no thought to the person clinging to that single thread. You hurry off, find somebody else, and make yourself happy... How could anyone forgive that? And yet the one you left behind has no right to complain.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そう……参考になる、なあ……ははは」
lines.english: “I-I see... Very... informative. Ha ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうだね、私も恋愛するときに役立てよーっと。あは、あははっ……さて、それじゃあ次は、冷凍食品のおいしい食べ方について話そっか――」
lines.english: “Y-yes, I'll keep that in mind if I ever fall in love. Ah ha... ha ha... Now, why don't we discuss the best way to prepare frozen food—”

lines.japanese: 「なあ、いま便利な呪文とか言ったか？　はッ、そりゃあテメエが都合のいい解釈してただけなんじゃねえの」
lines.english: “Did you call it a convenient spell? Hah. Maybe you're the one who heard what she wanted to hear.”

lines.japanese: 「――レン、ジで……チン、するときに……」
lines.english: “—When... heating it... in the micro... wave...”

lines.japanese: 「都合のいい解釈……針生さんって、面白いこと言うんだね」
lines.english: “Heard what I wanted... Hariu, you say the most amusing things.”

lines.japanese: にわかに空気が重くなった。俺と渡来明日香は、和平を促す言葉が見つけられずに、ただおろおろと身を寄せあった。
lines.english: The air abruptly grew heavy. Unable to find a single word that might restore peace, Asuka Watarai and I merely huddled together in confusion.

lines.japanese: 「だったらいっそのこと、介錯してくれればいいのに……どうしてわざわざ希望を残そうとするの……？」
lines.english: “Then they should have finished me off cleanly... Why go out of their way to leave me hope...?”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃ、相手にも都合ってモンがあンじゃないのォ。その待ってる間に、同じ場所で愚図愚図してるか、相手と同じ高みを目指すか……要は自分次第って話」
lines.english: “Maybe the other person has circumstances of their own. While you wait, you can either sit there moping in the same place or strive to reach the same heights... The point is, that’s up to you.”

lines.japanese: 「苦しんでる相手の気持ちは無視なんだ」
lines.english: “So the feelings of the one in pain don't matter.”

lines.japanese: 「自分の都合に、相手を合わせるなよ」
lines.english: “Don't demand that somebody else arrange their life for your convenience.”

lines.japanese: 「それなら最初から好きだなんて言うなよ豚野郎」
lines.english: “Then don't tell me you love me in the first place, you pig!”

lines.japanese: 「あわ、あわわわわ……」
lines.english: “W-whoa, whoa, whoa...”

lines.japanese: まずい、山科京の目がまずい色に……
lines.english: This was bad. Miyako Yamashina's eyes were turning a very bad color...

lines.japanese: たたた、助けてくれ渡来明日香。おまえは山科京の友達──
lines.english: H-help us, Asuka Watarai! You're Miyako Yamashina's friend—

lines.japanese: ──って、いねえー！
lines.english: —She's gone!

lines.japanese: やつはいつの間にか、テーブルの隅で『カラッと揚げよう！　なるほど乙女の冷凍食品』を熟読中だった。つまり逃げた。
lines.english: At some point, she'd retreated to the corner of the table and buried herself in *Fry It Crisp! The Maiden's Guide to Frozen Food*. In other words, she fled.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君はどうするの」
lines.english: “What would you do, Haneda?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: そして戦禍は俺にまで飛び火してきた。
lines.english: And now the war had spread to me.

lines.japanese: どうするって、何が……ああ、そういやこの事態、発端は俺のネタ振りだったっけ。ゆえあって付きあえない男女の話。
lines.english: What would I do about what...? Oh, right. I'd started this whole mess with my setup. The man and woman who couldn't be together because of circumstances.

lines.japanese: 「い、いや、だからさっきのは俺の話じゃなくて、あくまで例えとして……」
lines.english: “L-like I said, that wasn't about me. It was only an example...”

lines.japanese: 「でも悩んではいるんだよね？　その気持ちを相手は知るべき？　それとも自分ひとりのものでいいの？」
lines.english: “But you are troubled, aren't you? Should the other person know how you feel, or should those feelings belong to you alone?”

lines.japanese: 「げらげらげら。なんで選択肢が自分中心のものしかねえんだよ。狭い世界で生きてんなァ」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha ha! Why are both choices about you? You live in one cramped little world.”

lines.japanese: うわああああ。誰か、誰か助けてくれえ。
lines.english: Aaaaaah! Somebody, anybody, help me!

lines.japanese: しかし振りむいても、渡来明日香は本を開いたまま、物理的に不自然な角度へ首を曲げているだけだった。
lines.english: But when I turned, Asuka Watarai merely held her book open and bent her neck at a physically impossible angle.

lines.japanese: 「答えて羽田君」
lines.english: “Answer me, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「羽田ァ？」
lines.english: “Hanedaaa?”

lines.japanese: く、くそう、やむを得ん……山科京を傷つけるわけにはいかないし、ここは言いだしっぺの俺が覚悟を決めるか。
lines.english: D-damn it. I had no choice. I couldn't let Miyako Yamashina get hurt. As the man who had started this, I would have to steel myself.

lines.japanese: 「お、おれっ、実は妹萌えとか少女趣味に興味あるんだ！」
lines.english: “I-I'm actually into little sisters and younger girls!”

lines.japanese: 覚悟を決めた俺は、腹を割って真実を明かした。
lines.english: My resolve hardened, I opened my heart and revealed the truth.

lines.japanese: 「それはちょっと」
lines.english: “That's a little...”

lines.japanese: 「きも。うわ、きもっ」
lines.english: “Gross. Wow. That's gross.”

lines.japanese: 「どん引きだよね」
lines.english: “Total turnoff.”

lines.japanese: 満場一致の大不評だった。
lines.english: My confession met unanimous disapproval.

lines.japanese: そのまま三人は身を寄せ、俺の顔を窺いながらぼそぼそと囁きあっていた。
lines.english: The three of them huddled together and whispered while peeking at my face.

lines.japanese: で、でもいいんだ……羽田班にチームワークが戻ったなら、ぼくはそれで……。
lines.english: B-but that's okay... If I've restored teamwork to Team Haneda, then that's enough for me...

lines.japanese: あ！　でも俺ほんとは、シスコンとかロリコンとか全然ないからね？
lines.english: Oh! But I don't actually have a sister complex or a Lolita complex or anything, okay?

lines.japanese: さて、今日の帰りはどうしようかな。
lines.english: Now then. What should I do after school today?

lines.japanese: 俺はケータイを開いて時間を確認しながら、アフタースクールの予定を考えていた。
lines.english: I flipped open my cell phone, checked the time, and considered my afternoon plans.

lines.japanese: 今日は火曜日かあ。早く帰って小鳩の顔が見たいなあ。タカシの俺が好きだったアニメ『生天使ノンドームちゃん』の二期も始まってるしなあ。
lines.english: It was Tuesday. I wanted to hurry home and see Kobato. The second season of *Bareback Angel Non-Dome*, an anime Takashi had loved, was airing too.

lines.japanese: ああ、だけど森里君と買い物に行くのもいいなあ。予定空いてるかなあ。うん、空いてるよね、なにしろ森里君だし。スケジュールすっかすかに違いないよね。
lines.english: But shopping with Morisato sounded good too. I wondered if he was free. Of course he was. This was Morisato, after all. His schedule was bound to be wide open.

lines.japanese: なんて期待を膨らませていたら、急に震えだすケータイ。
lines.english: Just as I was getting my hopes up, my phone started vibrating.

lines.japanese: アレキサンダー店長、軽部狩男氏からのメールだった。
lines.english: It was an email from Karuo Karube, the manager of Alexander.

lines.japanese: なんだろう。とりあえず添付してある画像は見る前に即刻削除して……なに、シフトに穴が空いた？
lines.english: What could he want? First, I immediately deleted the attached image without opening it... Oh? He had a gap in the schedule?

lines.japanese: アレキサンダーでのアルバイト期間は１２月で一応終わっている。だが今日みたいに突然欠員が出たときは、軽部店長から声をかけられることがあった。
lines.english: My stint working at Alexander had technically ended in December. But when someone called out without warning, as they had today, Manager Karube occasionally asked me to fill in.

lines.japanese: どうやらアレキサンダー常勤の大学生・工藤さんに急用が出来たらしい。可能ならその穴埋めに来てほしいとのこと。
lines.english: Apparently Kudou, one of Alexander's regular college-student employees, had something urgent come up. The manager wanted me to cover if I could.

lines.japanese: ふむ、これは好都合。最近の俺は、小鳩のケータイのためにバリバリ稼ぎたいお年頃だからな。
lines.english: Hmm. This was perfect. I'd reached the age when a man wanted to work his fingers to the bone to buy Kobato a cell phone.

lines.japanese: 決まりだ。森里君との寄り道や小鳩との一時も魅力的だけど、工藤さんにはクローズ作業を基礎から教えてもらった恩もあるし。
lines.english: That settled it. A detour with Morisato or time with Kobato was tempting, but I also owed Kudou for teaching me the closing routine from the ground up.

lines.japanese: というわけで、俺は軽部店長に了解の旨を伝えると、急いで昇降口へ向かった。
lines.english: I sent Manager Karube my acceptance and hurried toward the shoe lockers.

lines.japanese: よし、誰かの役に立てる上に、アレキサンダーのみんなにも会えるぞ！　ははは、わくわくするなあ！
lines.english: Excellent. I could help somebody and see everyone at Alexander! Ha ha ha. I was getting excited!

lines.japanese: 「羽田ぁー」
lines.english: “Hanedaaa!”
“Hmm?”

lines.japanese: やる気に燃えていた俺を呼びとめる声ひとつ。俺はくるりと振りかえった。
lines.english: A voice stopped me in my tracks as I burned with motivation. I spun around.

lines.japanese: 「あれ、副委員長」
lines.english: “Oh, Vice Rep.”

lines.japanese: そこにいたのは我が組の女子学級委員、高内昌子だった。
lines.english: It was Masako Takauchi, the female class representative of our class.

lines.japanese: 「偶然じゃん。なに、羽田もいま帰るとこなん」
lines.english: “What a coincidence. What, you heading home now too, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「ああそうだ！　三学期初めての学校だからな、放課後への期待も膨らむだろう」
lines.english: “I am! It's the first school day of the third term. Naturally, one's expectations for the afternoon swell!”

lines.japanese: 「おー、よく分かんねーけど、なんか楽しそうじゃん」
lines.english: “Okay. Dunno what you mean, but you sure look like you're having fun.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうなんだ。放課後をどう楽しく過ごしてやろうか、わくわくしてるぞ！」
lines.english: “I am. I can hardly wait to see what manner of fun the afternoon holds!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、マジで？　んじゃ今からどっか寄ったりすんだ？」
lines.english: “Oh, seriously? You stopping somewhere on the way home, then?”

lines.japanese: 「だったら私、新しい茶店とかこないだ見つけてさ。中覗いてみたかったんだけど、ひとりじゃ入りにくくてー」
lines.english: “Well, I found this new café the other day. I've been wanting to check it out, but it's kinda hard to go in alone.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　そうなのか？」
lines.english: “Hmm? Is that so?”

lines.japanese: 高内昌子ともあろう者が、ずいぶん弱気なことを言うもんだ。ひとりでアマゾンの奥地にでも行けるタイプだと思っていたが。
lines.english: That sounded awfully timid for Masako Takauchi. I'd taken her for the sort who could venture alone into the heart of the Amazon.

lines.japanese: 「まあ羽田が暇だっつーなら、連れてってやんねーこともないけど」
lines.english: “Well, if you're free, I guess I wouldn't mind taking you along.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうなんだ。だけど俺は今日、アルバイトがあるんだ」
lines.english: “Oh, I see. But I have work today.”

lines.japanese: 残念だ、せっかくクラスメイトが誘ってくれたというのに。
lines.english: What a shame. A classmate had gone to the trouble of inviting me.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そーなん？」
lines.english: “Oh. You do?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、だからごめんね高内さん」
lines.english: “Yeah. Sorry, Takauchi.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　なに謝ってんの？　べつに？　暇なら連れてってやるかーってだけだし？　べつに羽田が居ても居なくてもカンケーねーし」
lines.english: “Huh? What're you apologizing for? Whatever. I was only gonna take you if you were free. Makes no difference to me whether you're there or not.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、いいや。そんなら別のやつ誘うし」
lines.english: “Fine. I'll invite somebody else.”

lines.japanese: 「そんな。俺もまた誘ってよ高内さん」
lines.english: “Don't say that. Ask me again sometime, Takauchi.”

lines.japanese: 友達百人ほしい俺は、誰の誘いだってバッチリ受けちゃうぞ。予定さえ合えばね。
lines.english: I wanted a hundred friends, so I was ready to accept anybody's invitation—as long as my schedule allowed.

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、そう……ま、そこまで言うなら、また今度誘ってやるけどさ」
lines.english: “Huh. Okay... Well, if you want it that bad, I'll invite you again sometime.”

lines.japanese: 彼女はさっさと靴を履いて出てゆく。外で顔見知りの下級生を見つけたようだ。
lines.english: She quickly put on her shoes and left. Outside, she seemed to spot a younger student she knew.

lines.japanese: 「おー、林田ちょうどいいとこに。ちっと話あンだけど付きあえよ」
lines.english: “Hey, Hayashida. Great timing. I gotta talk to you. Come with me.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、高内先輩、どうしたんです？」
lines.english: “Oh, Takauchi. What's up?”

lines.japanese: 「萌えって何なん？　なんか分かったことねーの」
lines.english: “What’s this whole ‘melts your heart’ thing, anyway? You figure anything out?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、萌えですか？　えっと、この前クラスの子に聞いたら、お弁当とか自分で作ると萌えーって言うらしいですよ」
lines.english: “Oh, that? Um, I asked a girl in my class the other day. Apparently making your own lunch melts people’s hearts.”

lines.japanese: 「は、なにそれ？　弁当？　はー、なるほどねえ」
lines.english: “Huh? What's that mean? Lunch? Ohhh. I get it.”

lines.japanese: ふーむ、後輩と歓談しながら下校とは高内昌子め、楽しそうなアフタースクールじゃないか。俺も見習いたいところだ。
lines.english: Hmm. Walking home while chatting with an underclassman? Masako Takauchi was having a fine afternoon. I could learn from her example.

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ俺は軽部店長が待ってるだろうし、アレキサンダーへ行くか！」
lines.english: “Well, Manager Karube is probably waiting. Off to Alexander!”

lines.japanese: アルバイトだって楽しいことは山ほどあるに違いない。それに、小鳩のために働くと思えば気力もみなぎるってもんだ。
lines.english: A shift at work surely held all kinds of fun. And when I thought of working for Kobato, energy surged through me.

lines.japanese: 俺はもりもり気持ちを高めながら花水木通りへ足を向けた。
lines.english: With my enthusiasm growing by the second, I set off for Flowering Dogwood Street.
